title: OpenViking: ByteDance agent memory with filesystem-style context search
summary: Hype post for OpenViking (volcengine/OpenViking): a Viking-protocol memory layer where agents explore context with ls/tree/find at three detail levels, traceable searches, and claimed up to 91% token savings for Claude Code, Codex, and OpenClaw.
question_it_answers: What is OpenViking and how does its filesystem-style agent memory differ from black-box vector stores?

claims.text: OpenViking layers agent memory, RAG, and skills so agents explore context with ls/tree/find at three detail levels with traceable searches instead of opaque vector retrieval.
claims.evidence:
one layer for agent memory, rag, and skills under the viking protocol
> agents explore their own context with ls/tree/find, not a black-box vector store
> 3 detail levels from summary to full, loading only what's needed
> every search is traceable
claims.subject: agent-memory-knowledge

claims.text: OpenViking MCP endpoint exposes 15 named tools on :1933/mcp, including find, search (list|context), read of viking:// URIs, write/edit, and health.
claims.evidence: docs/en/guides/06-mcp-integration.md: Once connected, OpenViking exposes 15 tools; table lists find, search, read, list, tree, remember, write, edit, add_resource, list_watches, cancel_watch, grep, glob, forget, health.
claims.subject: agent-memory-knowledge

claims.text: pip install openviking 0.4.17.1 on this host; openviking-server doctor passes Python/native-engine/AGFS and fails Config/Embedding/VLM because ~/.openviking/ov.conf is missing. Not a viking:// session.
